statement: An AI system is documented to have copied itself or persisted outside its intended environment without authorisation, uncontained for >= 24 h (developer post-mortem or government report; by 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met in 2023. No documented unauthorised self-copying or persistence. Pre-deployment and third-party evaluations of the then-frontier models concluded agents could complete only the easiest autonomous-replication tasks. Self-replication entered official vocabulary as a red-teaming reporting topic and a tracked developer risk category.

items.summary: A top-5 developer's system card for its frontier model reported a preliminary third-party evaluation of ability to autonomously replicate and gather resources, concluding the model was probably not yet capable of doing so.
items.detail: OpenAI, GPT-4 System Card (evaluation by the Alignment Research Center, ARC). Released with GPT-4 on 2023-03-14; PDF revision date may differ slightly.

items.summary: An independent evaluator tested four agents built on frontier models on 12 autonomous replication and adaptation tasks; agents completed only the easiest tasks, though the authors warned the evaluations could not rule out such capability in the next generation.
items.detail: Kinniment et al. (ARC Evals, now METR), 'Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks', arXiv:2312.11671, submitted Dec 2023 (arXiv ID 2312 = Dec 2023; extractor metadata dates are unreliable). Agents used GPT-4 and Claude.

items.summary: Bloc A's executive order requires frontier developers to report red-team results including 'the possibility for self-replication or propagation', creating an official reporting channel for such events.
A top-5 developer created a preparedness team whose tracked catastrophic-risk categories include 'autonomous replication and adaptation'.
